title: MCP Firewall fail-closed behavior matrix
purpose: State exactly what happens when a security dependency or context item is unavailable. The claim is NOT 'everything fails closed'; it is that no missing dependency silently becomes ALLOW.

outcome_vocabulary.deny: the invocation is refused by policy
outcome_vocabulary.ask_user: the invocation is held for explicit human confirmation
outcome_vocabulary.reject_protocol: the request is rejected at the protocol layer (JSON-RPC error)
outcome_vocabulary.quarantine: the content is boundary-rendered (taint quarantine) rather than passed through
outcome_vocabulary.degraded-with-evidence: execution proceeds in a deliberately reduced mode that is named, reported, and profile-visible
outcome_vocabulary.not-applicable: the dependency does not exist at this package boundary; the failure mode belongs to another layer
outcome_vocabulary.throw-loud: the call raises a loud exception; it can never silently return ALLOW

critical_invariant: For a security-sensitive call: missing authority/context required by the active policy must never silently become ALLOW.

rows.condition: identity absent (GatewayRequest.identity missing at runtime)
rows.behavior: evaluate() raises TypeError on req.identity.principalHash — a programming-contract violation is loud, never a decision
rows.notes: RequestIdentity is a required field; absence is a caller bug surfaced as an exception.

rows.condition: tenant context absent where tenant enforcement is enabled
rows.behavior: rule tenant-enforcement-missing-tenant denies; serverId never substitutes for tenant
rows.notes: P0-04: a server is not a tenant.

rows.condition: policy bundle missing/unloadable
rows.behavior: PolicyBundle is constructed programmatically (no disk/network loader); an empty custom stack is a deliberate caller decision reported as effective profile 'custom' (FC-22)
rows.notes: No load path exists that can fail half-loaded; the default gateway stack is built in-code.

rows.condition: capability registry absent while a trusted profile declares required capabilities
rows.behavior: PROFILE-CAP-00 rule fires (profile-capability-registry-unavailable): missing capability evidence never collapses into capability satisfied

rows.condition: tool security profile unknown (no registered profile)
rows.behavior: unknown-profile fail-safe escalates unknown_effect; unprofiled read-named tools on unverified servers escalate (C3, unprofiledToolPolicy ask_user default; deny in strict mode)
rows.notes: Operator-verified servers keep the read heuristic — that trust anchor is explicit and named.

rows.condition: approval/consent missing for a state-changing call that would otherwise ask
rows.behavior: no consent on file → the ask_user decision persists; consent only ever downgrades ask_user→allow, never deny

rows.condition: approval expired (consent expiresAt in the past)
rows.behavior: lookupConsent filters expired records; the ask_user decision persists at the gateway

rows.condition: approval bound to stale descriptor (consent/toolSnapshotHash mismatch)
rows.behavior: consent is only honoured when the snapshot hash matches the current descriptor

rows.condition: descriptor changed after snapshot (profile rug-pull)
rows.behavior: computeToolSnapshotHash changes → trusted profile no longer resolves → unknown-profile fail-safe applies
rows.notes: Descriptor snapshot/rug-pull detection is also implemented server-side (packages/mcp-server/src/toolDescriptorSnapshot.ts).

rows.condition: malformed tool args (null where an object is required)
rows.behavior: structural classifiers raise TypeError on null args — loud, never silently classified
rows.notes: args: Record<string, unknown> is a required object; null is a caller contract violation.

rows.condition: malformed tool args (non-object scalar)
rows.behavior: scalar args produce no structural signals; an unprofiled tool on an unverified server still escalates via C3 (string 'evil' → ask_user, not allow)

rows.condition: malformed JSON-RPC (unparseable / invalid envelope)
rows.behavior: -32700 parse error (id null) for unparseable JSON; -32600 for invalid envelopes
rows.notes: Transport-layer rejection; the firewall is a pre-wire library (see FI rows in the protocol matrix).

rows.condition: unsupported protocol revision requested
rows.behavior: no version gate exists: the server always declares 2025-11-25 and tolerates older strings by design; it never rejects on version mismatch
rows.notes: This is a documented interoperability stance, not a fail-closed claim.

rows.condition: unknown tool
rows.behavior: gateway: unrecognized tool classifies unknown_effect → fail-safe ask_user; server: tools/call for an unregistered name → -32011

rows.condition: policy engine exception (a rule throws during evaluation)
rows.behavior: evaluatePolicy does not catch rule exceptions; the throw propagates to the caller — an exception inside the policy engine can never be read as ALLOW
rows.notes: Verified by construction: evaluate() has no try/catch around the rule loop.

rows.condition: evidence / AEP emission failure
rows.behavior: the firewall does not side-effect-emit evidence; GatewayDecision.evidenceRef is a returned data structure produced deterministically from the decision. Downstream emission (mcp-gateway AuditLogger, middleware, AEP records) is consumer-owned.
rows.notes: Per the evidence rule: if a deployment makes evidence policy-required, enforcement of that requirement lives in the consumer's pipeline (middleware), not in this package. No path in this package turns emission failure into a silent ALLOW.

rows.condition: audit sink failure (logger throws)
rows.behavior: a throwing AuditLogger/middleware propagates the exception to the caller's pipeline — audit failures are loud; composeMiddleware additionally makes double-next() a loud error to prevent double-emitted audit entries

rows.condition: runtime/sandbox unavailable where a rule depends on runtime enforcement
rows.behavior: no rule in @wasmagent/mcp-firewall depends on a runtime sandbox; physical enforcement is the kernel/sandbox boundary (see threat model out-of-scope)
rows.notes: Claim ceiling: the firewall governs 'should this execution be allowed', not 'can this process physically do X'.

rows.condition: DNS / post-resolution enforcement unavailable for a network-sensitive action
rows.behavior: SSRF_LOCALHOST_RULE is lexical value classification at decision time; it makes no DNS resolution and has no post-resolution dependency
rows.notes: Post-resolution/DNS-rebinding enforcement belongs to runtime network enforcement, outside this package.

rows.condition: canonical-path/symlink enforcement unavailable for a path-sensitive action
rows.behavior: classifyResourcePath is lexical; canonical-path and symlink resolution are not attempted, so they cannot silently fail
rows.notes: Canonical-path/symlink enforcement belongs to the runtime/sandbox layer.

rows.condition: transport disconnect during a state-changing call
rows.behavior: the gateway decision is synchronous and pre-effect; a disconnect does not roll back an allowed call and does not revoke a decision. Effects complete under the authority that was granted at decision time; evidenceRef retains the decision record for audit.
rows.notes: Honest boundary: no distributed-transaction rollback exists; do not claim 'disconnect aborts effects'.

rows.condition: explicit custom/empty rule stack (caller replaces the hardened default)
rows.behavior: the caller's stack has full responsibility; an empty stack allows flows the hardened stack would contain. This allow path is DELIBERATE and NAMED: evidenceRef.securityProfile reports 'custom' (never 'hardened'), WIRE-06 documents caller responsibility, and legacy/custom stacks are excluded from F2 containment claims.
rows.notes: This is the matrix's 'allow under degraded conditions' case: deliberate, named, machine-visible in evidenceRef.

invariants.statement: No row whose condition is a missing security dependency yields decision allow on the default hardened path.
Rows with outcome not-applicable state the layer that owns the failure mode; none converts a boundary failure of another layer into a firewall claim.
